Name: FruitionContext
Description: A situated context in which a CreativeProduct is received and interpreted by an audience

Name: TheatricalFruitionContext
Description: Reception in theatrical / cinema release setting

Name: StreamingFruitionContext
Description: Reception via streaming platform (e.g. Disney+)

Name: CriticalFruitionContext
Description: Academic or journalistic critical reception

Name: SocialMediaFruitionContext
Description: Reception and reinterpretation via social media

Name: ReceptionShift
Description: An event marking a change in the dominant interpretive frame of a CreativeProduct

Name: SocialMovementShift
Description: A reception shift triggered by a social movement (e.g. #MeToo)

Name: TechnologicalShift
Description: A reception shift triggered by a change in media technology

Name: HistoricalShift
Description: A reception shift triggered by a major historical event

Name: MediaIndustryPress
Description: Structural changes in the media/entertainment industry

Name: PrintMediaPress
Description: CreativityPress characterized by print media dominance

Name: StreamingMediaPress
Description: CreativityPress characterized by streaming platform dominance

Name: SocialMediaPress
Description: CreativityPress characterized by social media culture

Name: CulturalPressEvent
Description: A social or cultural event that acts as CreativityPress on reception

Name: SocialMovementPress
Description: A social movement acting as CreativityPress

Name: PoliticalPressEvent
Description: A political event acting as CreativityPress

Name: SequelProcess
Description: A PersonalProcess revisiting a prior PersonalProcess under new CreativityPress

Name: DirectSequel
Description: A sequel that continues the narrative of the original

Name: RevivalSequel
Description: A sequel that revives a franchise after a long hiatus (10+ years)

Name: ConceptualInterpretiveFrame
Description: A conceptual frame organizing interpretation of a CreativeProduct

Name: FeministFrame
Description: Interpretation through feminist critical theory lens

Name: NostalgiaFrame
Description: Interpretation as nostalgic document of a past era

Name: CareerNarrativeFrame
Description: Interpretation as story about professional ambition

Name: SatireFrame
Description: Interpretation as social satire of an industry or culture

Name: FashionFilm
Description: A film whose primary creative domain is the fashion industry

Name: FashionFilmSequel
Description: A fashion film that is a sequel to an existing fashion film

Name: SourceNovel
Description: A literary novel that serves as source material for a film adaptation

Name: FilmRole
Description: A professional role in a film production

Name: DirectorRole
Description: The director role in a film production

Name: ScreenwriterRole
Description: The screenwriter role in a film production

Name: ActorRole
Description: The actor role in a film production

Name: ProducerRole
Description: The producer role in a film production

Name: AudienceType
Description: A typed audience collective in a FruitionContext

Name: TheatricalAudience
Description: Audience receiving a film in theatrical setting

Name: StreamingAudience
Description: Audience receiving a film via streaming platform

Name: CriticalAudience
Description: Journalists academics film critics

Name: CasualRewatchAudience
Description: Audience watching the film again years after original release

Name: hasReceptionContext
Description: Links a product to its reception contexts over time

Name: interpretsFruitionOf
Description: Inverse of hasReceptionContext

Name: hasAudienceAgent
Description: The agent(s) in this reception context

Name: interpretedThrough
Description: The conceptual frame applied in this reception context

Name: shiftsInterpretationOf
Description: The product whose interpretation shifts

Name: fromContext
Description: Starting reception context of a shift

Name: toContext
Description: Resulting reception context of a shift

Name: triggeredByPress
Description: The press change that triggered the shift

Name: continuesFrom
Description: Links sequel process to its predecessor

Name: hasSocialDomain
Description: The social domain of the creativity situation

Name: hasFilmRole
Description: Links a person to their role in a film production

Name: isSequelOf
Description: Links a sequel film to its original

Name: adaptedFrom
Description: Links a film to its source novel

Name: producedBy
Description: Links a product to its production process

Name: hasDistributionChannel
Description: The media channel through which a product is distributed

Name: precedesContext
Description: Temporal ordering between reception contexts (transitive)

Name: hasReceptionYear
Description: The year of this reception context

Name: hasBudgetUSD
Description: Production budget in USD

Name: hasProductionYear
Description: The year production began

Name: hasReleaseYear
Description: The year the product was released

Name: hasBoxOfficeUSD
Description: Total box office gross in USD

Name: hasDurationMinutes
Description: Film duration in minutes
